summary: Guidance requested to safely retract batching/caching/quantization changes after production latency spike
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden 2-3x tail latency increase for text-generation requests after enabling a combined optimizer profile (dynamic batching + KV prefetch + q4 quant profile) at 2026-03-10T21:00:00Z. The spike began ~10 minutes after the change and persisted until a temporary binary toggle was applied by the customer to disable dynamic batching.

Impact:
- A subset (~7%) of production requests for NeuroDocs experienced >5s tail latency, causing intermittent client timeouts and degraded UX for end users.
- No 5xx errors observed; error rate unchanged.
- Billing unaffected.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-7
- Region: us-west (primary), us-east fallback
- Models: redwood-v2-small (serving runtime with quantized variant open-7B-quantized)
- Traffic pattern: mix of short (<=64 tokens) and long (<=1024 tokens) requests, 70% short.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Apply optimizer profile: enable dynamic batching (max_batch=64, target_latency_ms=30), enable KV prefetch for short-prefix caching, apply q4 quantization profile from policy v2026-03-09.
2) Route normal traffic for 10+ minutes.
3) Observe latency distribution via Console per-route percentiles and runtime traces.

Observed behavior:
- 95th/99th percentile latencies rose from 120ms/240ms to 900ms/2800ms respectively for affected routes.
- Span traces show increased queuing in the batching actor and occasional GPU kernel stalls when switching between quant paths.
- KV cache metrics show increased miss rate after the profile applied (unexpected).

Expected behavior:
- Modest latency improvement or small regression during warmup, not multi-second tail spikes.

Logs / measurements:
- Console trace links: https://console.redwood.ai/trace/abcd1234 (samples attached in linked_confluence)
- Serving runtime logs attached: serving_runtime_usw-2026-03-10-21.tar.gz (uploaded to customer bucket)

Immediate mitigation attempted by customer:
- Toggle dynamic batching OFF via console feature flag at 2026-03-10T21:12:12Z — partially restored baseline tail latency after ~90s.
- Rolled back quantization to previous q8-lite profile in a canary at 2026-03-10T21:30:00Z — no immediate further improvement.

Request:
Customer requests an action plan for a safe, stepwise retraction of the combined optimizations and recommendations to avoid regression when reapplying optimizer settings. They prefer a playbook that can be executed during low-traffic windows and that includes verification checkpoints and fallbacks.
comments: 2026-03-11 09:05 Priya Shah (Support): Logged on behalf of NeuroDocs. Customer provided runtime logs and percentile graphs. Asked for an engineer to assist with safe retraction steps and recommended verification queries.

2026-03-11 10:40 Ethan Morgan (SRE): Acknowledged. Will coordinate with runtime team. Initial ask: can you confirm if the KV prefetch rule was enabled for long-requests or short-only? Also requested sample client requests (redacted).
2026-03-11 11:12 Alex Wu (Customer, NeuroDocs): KV prefetch was enabled globally via the profile. Uploaded sample payloads to the secure share.

2026-03-12 08:22 Ethan Morgan (SRE): Preliminary analysis: traces indicate batching actor queuing increases when batcher switches between sequence-length groups; quantized kernel selection shows occasional fallback to a slower path when sequence >256 tokens. Hypothesis: combined optimizer profile created cross-cutting state which increases cold-path transitions and causes increased miss activity in KV prefetch. Proposing controlled retraction steps.
2026-03-12 12:10 Priya Shah (Support): Shared proposed stepwise plan with customer for approval. Scheduled low-traffic window 2026-03-13 02:00-03:00 UTC.
2026-03-13 02:05 Alex Wu (Customer): Approved. Ready for guided retraction.
investigation_notes: 01) Reproducer: In staging, enabling the same optimizer profile with synthetic mixture traffic reproduced tail-latency pattern after ~6-8 minutes.

02) Batching internals: batcher policy uses dynamic grouping heuristics; when short and long requests interleave, it frequently flushes and re-evaluates groups causing queuing spikes under high concurrency.

03) KV prefetch: prefetch warmup policy assumes stable token prefix distribution; profile enabled global prefetch which increased competition for cache slots leading to higher eviction and miss churn.

04) Quantization pathing: our kernel selector currently has a fallback for sequences >256 that is not yet specialized for q4; this causes occasional CPU-bound copy/reshape operations increasing latency.
05) No CPU/GPU OOMs or 5xx; GPU utilization did not exceed 85% but observed micro-pauses correlating with quant-path transitions.
06) Logs referenced: serving_runtime_usw-2026-03-10-21/worker-12.log shows repeated 'kernel_fallback: sequence_over_threshold' messages aligned with tail spikes.
07) Related prior tickets: SUP-42760 (kv-prefetch-quant-failsafe) contains a similar prefetch eviction pattern; reuse portions of that playbook.
08) Risk assessment: safe to perform retraction in stages; avoid a full simultaneous revert of all optimizer toggles to allow post-change verification.
recommended_stepwise_playbook: Step A (Pre-checks, 30m): Verify canary baseline; take a runtime snapshot; confirm alerting thresholds and rollback playbook available; notify stakeholders and schedule low-traffic window.

Step B (Disable KV prefetch global -> short-only, 5-10m): Change prefetch scope from global to short-prefix-only and monitor cache hitrate and p95/p99 for 15 minutes. If tail latency remains elevated, proceed to Step C.

Step C (Reduce batching aggressiveness, 5-10m): Set dynamic batching max_batch=16 and target_latency_ms=40 to reduce grouping churn. Monitor queuing metrics, request batching distribution, and p99 for 20 minutes.

Step D (Staged quantization revert, canary -> gradual): Revert q4 -> q8-lite in a 5% canary first, verify kernel paths do not trigger fallback, then incrementally increase canary to 25% and 100% with 15-minute observation windows between steps.

Step E (Full verification): After each change validate: console percentiles, trace samples for kernel fallback messages, KV hit/miss rates, GPU kernel stall traces. Maintain ability to re-enable previous setting within 2 minutes if regressions surface.

Step F (Post-mortem and configuration hygiene): Capture configuration diff, submit PR for a safer profile that scopes KV prefetch to short-only, adjusts batching heuristics, and tags quantization path thresholds. Recommend adding a runtime guard that prevents simultaneous enabling of global prefetch + aggressive batching on fleets with mixed sequence distributions.

Rollback safety notes: Do not revert all optimizations at once. Apply one change at a time with defined observability checks and time horizons. Keep a pinned route to a known-good model variant for instant fallback.
Verification queries: list of 6 post-change checks to run in Console (p50/p95/p99, batch size distribution, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_count, GPU stall events, end-to-end tail latency percentiles).

Estimated time for full retraction (safe mode): ~90-120 minutes including staging, canarying, and verifications. Emergency immediate toggle (if customer prefers) available but higher risk of transient errors.
next_steps: 1) Execute Playbook Steps A-B in scheduled window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC with SRE on call.
2) SRE to run canary for Step D only after Steps B and C if necessary.
3) Post-change, produce a short incident report and update customer-facing runbook with the safer optimizer profile.
4) Follow up with a product ask to add a runtime interlock preventing the specific combination that triggered this incident.
